chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

finally... a chapter count... subject to change of course but I'm working on the last four chapters now and the end is in sight after more than half a year of writing... can you believe I've been working on this since last December? I don't know how many of you have been here since I started posting in January but wow... it's been so long... the home stretch... I still have a ton of work to do before this is finished, so I won't be saying goodbye to this fic anytime soon, but I'm a little emotional ngl

The sun comes up. Mydei has been awake since long before it rose. Phainon does not wake even now. Mydei sits at the side of the bed, leaning forward with his elbows on his knees and listening to the soft, steady sound of Phainon's breath. He slides his hands into his hair, rubs his thumbs over his temples.

He's been on alert for too long, some kind of paranoid guard dog. Phainon is fine, the Flame Reaver is gone for now, and yet. He sighs, drops his hands, and unpicks the tie on the bandage around his wrist, unraveling it slow, coil by coil. There's a jagged, golden scab about the width of a finger, half healed by the Sign of Aquila. He traces it with his fingertips, trying not to think of Ptolemy.

Phainon continues to sleep, the blanket pulled up to his mouth, hair a mess, still dirty from his reckless training last night and getting the mess all over Mydei's sheets. He smells like stress, pain, sweat. He's smelled that way all night, no matter how dreamlessly and peacefully he seems to be sleeping, and maybe that's why Mydei hasn't been able to all night.

Fool, he thinks, watching the blanket rise and fall with Phainon's breath. You reckless, idiotic fool.

Quietly, he stands, finding the basin of water by his dresser and washing his wrist. On goes a thin layer of healing salve—Perdikkas' recipe—and a new bandage, which he wraps one-handed. Again, he looks at Phainon on the bed. Again, he finds him sleeping.

He sits back down, frustrated and impatient yet unwilling to leave his side or wake him up. His chest feels tight. When he closes his eyes, he sees Ptolemy again, remembers him scribing something into his journal once, Peucesta playing his lyre in the background, Hephaestion laughing with Perdikkas and Leonnius, the six of them warm by the fire.

"One day we'll all be some horrific part of history," he'd said. This had been one of the first winters they'd come back on their own, and one where they'd lost four of their number, the most of any season. Ptolemy had laughed, then, kind of of quiet. "Obviously I don't want to die any time soon, but I think... the sooner we can be forgotten, and no child will ever again go through what we did, the better."

"We're needed," Mydei had protested.

"Sure," Ptolemy agreed. "But the world will figure something else out. A trained sorcerer can do most of we can anyway."

"And what about all of our knowledge? What happens when all of that is lost?"

"Someone will find it." He paused to think. "Maybe we'll make a pact. The last of us will take all our books to the Grove of Epiphany, that way the knowledge can last."

This was years ago, but even now he thinks about this exchange. Them, who suffered. Them, who have dedicated their lives to killing the monsters plaguing the people, forced into becoming monsters themselves, hated for things outside their control. He's known for a long time that their era is coming to an end.

Five of them left. Maybe these five will live another fifty years on the Path, but even then... Kremnos is crumbling. They're so few. They've all been prepared for a while now, for this legacy to die.

Faint stirring. Phainon, still groggy and soft with sleep, tugging the blanket down a little, eyes cracking open. Mydei looks at him, his mess of hair, his bleary eyes, bluer than anything even at a time like this. "Good morning," Mydei says, the first words he's spoken all day, even though he's been up for an age.

Phainon's eyes slip shut again. He breathes like he's losing the battle against sleep. His skin must be warm. Maybe under all of that stale scent of stress and pain and sweat, he'd smell like his usual self up close. Mydei watches him breathe for a moment, two, feeling like his insides are sticky without any way to give them a wash, and then Phainon sits up slow, eyes still shut, and pushes the blanket into his lap.

A little longer, his eyes peel open. He doesn't shiver at the cold, because Mydei has kept the fireplace going. "This is your room," he says, voice low and cracking with sleep.

"Yes," Mydei agrees. "I needed to be sure you wouldn't wake up in the night and decide on some more training."

He watches Phainon swallow, watches his gaze flick from place to place. His hands curl around his shins, legs pulling in and crossing. He looks awkward, guilty, and they haven't talked much, since the Flame Reaver came. He blames himself, Mydei knows. He blames himself for all of it, the burning of those towns, all the death, Ptolemy, their injuries. There's no way he doesn't, being the kind of person that he is.

They haven't talked much, but maybe they should have. Maybe Mydei should've... What? What is he supposed to say?

"I'm sorry," Phainon tries. He won't make eye contact, gaze turned toward the floor, so Mydei stares at his eyelashes. "I didn't— I know that was stupid of me last night, but I..."

"You want to be stronger," Mydei says, sighing. "I understand. But training like that, so hard that you pass out in weather like this, where you could've frozen to death— That's only going to make things worse."

"I know," Phainon says. "I know. I'm sorry." They're both quiet for a moment, two. "And thank you. For bringing me inside. For..."

"Don't thank me," Mydei says, bowing forward, elbows on knees. He remembers the weight of Phainon in his arms. The strain in his injured wrist, the tickle of hair against his throat. How cold Phainon had been. How Mydei had been scared more than anything else. "Just don't do it again."

"I thought you would be angry."

"What makes you so sure I'm not?"

"You... Well..." His gaze lifts, flicks right back away when it meets Mydei's. He laughs awkwardly, guiltily. "Maybe you are. Maybe you just handle it a lot better than I do."

Phainon, at that inn, getting right up in the innkeeper's face. Phainon, sleeping by his side in the stables, fighting for their meals. Phainon, furious at Okhema's gates. Mydei's mouth twitches at the corner, a little bit fond, a little bit bitter. "Was there ever any doubt about that?"

Another laugh, just as awkward as the first, the slightest bit warmer. "I suppose not," Phainon admits. A pause. "Listen, Mydei..." His mouth opens and closes like he can't find the words, and Mydei is so tired. He doesn't want to hear whatever Phainon might come up with, another apology or whatever else, so he reaches out and finds Phainon's hand, finding it warm instead of cold for once, pulling it to his forehead, bowing over it.

"Just. Shut up," he says, closing his eyes, exhaling everything in him. Phainon stays silent. His fingers twitch, and Mydei presses his forehead harder into them. "It's fine."

"I don't—" Phainon swallows. "Somehow I don't think it is." His palm sweats. Mydei shakes his head against Phainon's knuckles. "Mydei."

"Phainon," he says back, eyes still shut. He can imagine Phainon's expression. His wide eyes, his confusion. He must be entirely lost. Mydei can't bring himself to do a thing about it. To explain himself, to try and make sense of any of this. They don't do this, he knows, they shouldn't do this, but he can't make himself pull away.

"I'll take better care of myself," Phainon offers tentatively. "I won't— you won't have to find me like that again."

He's so aware of the beat of his own heart. He grinds his forehead into Phainon's knuckles and wonders why, out of all the hundreds of lives he's tried and failed to save, he thinks losing this one would break him the worst. For Phainon, for himself, for Ptolemy, he needs this to work out. He needs the city to not be crumbling down around them. He needs Phainon safe and happy and strong. He needs no one else to die. He needs all of them to be able to work together and do this.

"Make sure of that," he says, and stays like this a little longer. Too long, he knows. Too much, for how little they are.

"Mydei," Phainon says again, softer. A moment passes. Mydei can hear the pause in his breath, the slight shifting of fabric, and then Phainon places his hand not stolen on the back of Mydei's head, fingers threading lightly through his hair.

"HKS," Mydei murmurs, and does not move away. "What are you doing?"

But Phainon doesn't give him an answer, just leaves them in this odd space, Mydei bowed over their joined hands, Phainon petting his hair, all of it too soft and too much and not them at all. "I need to ask," Phainon says instead. "I realize with the mess that I made, I—" He stops, starts again on a new breath. "I need to know what happened, and whether there's a chance that it might happen again."

Slow, Mydei lifts his head. Phainon's hand slips, fingers skimming the braid behind his ear before it drops back into his lap. Their eyes meet. Again, Mydei remembers carrying him all the way here, cold and shivering, remembers how heavy he'd been, how heavy he'd made Mydei feel. He wonders if the truth might fix this. If the truth might make it worse.

"There are holes in the wards," he admits, sighing. "Not regular wear and tear; the Flame Reaver has been actively tearing them down. We thought we had it under control until Anaxa wakes up and can fix them, but... clearly not. We didn't want to tell you because..."

"—The more afraid I am, the stronger he gets," Phainon fills in, exhaling shakily. The muscles in his jaw shift as he clenches his teeth. "Right. So you lied to me."

"So we lied to you," Mydei agrees. They each hold their own shreds of guilt. Looking down, he opens his hand for Phainon's to go free, but finds his own squeezed harder instead.

"I'm sorry," Phainon says again, and when Mydei looks up, his expression is intense. "I'm sorry that you can't trust me to not be afraid. I'm sorry that I broke our promise when I didn't fight back. I'm sorry that—"

"And when would you have had the chance to?" Mydei cuts him off, squeezing back. "You showed up, felt that initial spike of panic, and then Castorice knocked you out. When would you have fought back if the scenario replayed itself? We didn't give you the chance." He watches Phainon's mouth open, close. "And we lied to you, so you thought you were safe here. We promised you the whole winter to prepare, and then you walk into that. In what world would it have made sense for you to be anything but terrified?"

"Ptolemy still died because of me," Phainon protests. "One of your closest friends, one of your brothers. Shouldn't you be furious at me?"

"If you're to blame, then so am I, so are we all," Mydei says, squeezing hard enough that he's sure Phainon's hand must hurt. "Ptolemy died because of our poor planning. You did nothing other than be born at the same time as a monster. Any fear you feel, it's only natural. The Flame Reaver would be a hundred times as strong were he bound to anyone else, how many times do I have to say that?"

"Fine," Phainon says, brows pulling together, voice wavering as he tries to contain frustration or something else. Again, "Fine. I'll accept that. But what if this happens again? Anaxagoras still hasn't recovered, I'm sure those holes in the wards are still there, and even if you guys managed to chase the Flame Reaver off, he'll be back."

"We'll fight him again," Mydei says, resolute as he can be. "And if that isn't enough, Anaxa will fix the wards, we'll spend the rest of the winter training, and we'll end this in the spring like we planned."

"It can't be that simple," Phainon says, shaking his head. "Mydei, you can't trust me not to make him stronger. The moment he shows up, I—"

"We didn't give you the chance to fight," Mydei cuts him off. "Next time, if we did, would you? Would you keep your promise to me?"

"I..." Phainon wets his lips, looks at their joined hands. "I would try," he says. "But—"

"Then it's enough," Mydei stops him. "You can't give up now, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae." He folds his other hand over both of theirs. "We'll make a plan, and this time you'll be in on it."

△

Even with all of them, it's a small group at the table in the dining hall. Mydei, Phainon, Castorice, Krateros, Peucesta, Hephaestion, Chartonus. Seven of them in this hall to seat hundreds. Anaxa is still absent. He's been waking long enough to take his meals, but he's fevered and manic and nothing out of his mouth makes sense before he passes right out again. At the very least, he doesn't seem to be in pain any longer.

It's clear now, that he'll recover. Mydei isn't sure how much energy the Flame Reaver had gotten from Phainon, but he should still be licking his wounds. Hopefully he will be long enough for Anaxa to recover. And hopefully the new mutation gives Anaxa the power he says it will.

A piece from the divine body of Cerces. It has to. It has to.

Titans above. If only they hadn't lost the tracking device during the fight. Then they wouldn't have to worry and wonder so much about whether or not the Flame Reaver is there. Mydei takes a breath, and runs through the plan.

"Krateros, I want you with Chartonus if the Flame Reaver shows up. Castorice, Peucesta, Hephaestion, and I will do the fighting; you two just focus on securing Anaxa and getting somewhere safe as far from the combat as possible. He's only after Phainon, so the odds of him going for you are fairly low."

"I would fight too, if I would be of use to you," Krateros says.

"No," Mydei says, shaking his head. "I didn't invite you here to needlessly lay down your life. I promised you safety in exchange for your stories and your help training Phainon. If I can help it, I don't want a scratch on you. Please, if you would, stay with Chartonus."

"Bite, I do not," says Chartonus, sitting politely even as he towers over them.

"I wasn't worried that you did, friend," Krateros says. "But very well. I will stay with Chartonus."

"The ward around the library is already broken; it's most likely that he'll come through there again, especially since we wounded him. He'll be weak; everyone should be wearing their armor at all times and keep weapons nearby. We'll need to set up barricades at all of the weak points. Castorice, I want you in charge of that. Chartonus, if you could help with the heavy lifting."

Castorice nods tightly. Chartonus gives his agreement.

"And Phainon—"

"I want to fight," Phainon says, glancing around the table. He lets out a breath, wilting. "But I will defer to your judgement if you think it's best that I find a place to hide instead."

"The problem," Hephaestion starts carefully, glancing at Mydei as if for permission, "is that we don't know whether that's really an option. If he shows up far away from you and we have time to get to him, then it might be best if you hide, but..."

"It's more likely that he'll try to skip past us and go straight to you," Mydei finishes. "He's realized we're a threat. You're the only way he can make himself stronger. I don't think he'll bother with us at all, if he can help it."

He watches Phainon swallow, throat bobbing against his choker. "Then I'll fight alongside you," he says, expression going steely. "And if it comes to it, Castorice can... sedate me, again."

"Trust in yourself," Peucesta adds softly. "You may not have magic or mutations on your side the way we do, but you're strong. We're all by your side. There's nothing to fear."

Phainon looks like he wants to say something to that, but he only exhales shakily and nods. "I will try," he says, squeezing his eyes shut and taking a deep breath. I can do this, he seems to say to himself. "This time, I'll be ready for him."

△

They walk out of the meeting emboldened. They're all half expecting the Flame Reaver to jump out around every corner, but he never does. Without the tracking device to confirm their safety, it's difficult to act normally, to find ways to pass the time as they would've. He's not sure if any of them will be able to sleep.

Someone stays with Phainon at all times; now it's Hephaestion or Peucesta. Mydei helps build the barricade in the librarian's office, the entire wall taken out. Blood still stains the ground, dried, crusting gold from the Flame Reaver and Ptolemy both.

Cold wind whips through the space no matter how high they build the barricade up. When it's done, hours later, Mydei crosses his arms around himself and sighs. No point in being here any longer. He leaves as Castrum Kremnos gives another groan, shaking the walls.

He finds Krateros in the biggest, best taken care of sitting room, taking a break after wearing himself out helping set up barricades too, reading a book by a lit fireplace. Somehow, he seems more at peace than any of them.

"Krateros," Mydei greets him.

A nod back, Krateros marks his place and shuts the book. "Son of Gorgo."

"You seem well-adjusted," Mydei says. "Is there anything I can do to make you more comfortable?"

A rough laugh. "I've told you before; I'm old and no longer fear death. I can see the guilt behind your eyes, and I'm telling you now, there's no need for it."

He's right. It sits, quiet and twisting in the pit of his stomach. Guilt for the danger, for that fact that his promises are breaking one by one along with the wards around Castrum Kremnos. "You were my mother's most trusted friend," he says. "I need you to be safe and well."

"You are your mother's son," Krateros says back. He looks Mydei over, never shying from the odd color of his eyes, the marks all over his skin. "She would've been proud of you."

Mydei, who must be so far removed from the son she'd imagined having. Mydei, the child of Destiny who killed his father and tore his parents' love apart. "I can only hope that she would," he says, and is surprised by the exhaustion in his own voice.

Krateros sets the book aside and stands, stiff and with some effort. "Come here, son," he says, and takes a couple of steps to bridge their gap. Mydei meets him halfway and finds himself pulled into an embrace. Krateros, still sturdy in his age, smelling like sword oil and soap. He claps Mydei on the back, squeezes him with surprising strength. "You're a good man, Mydeimos. I knew your mother well, and when I say she would be proud, be sure that I mean it."

Strange, this emotion that wells up. Mydei lifts his arms to return the embrace, and after only a moment longer it's over, Krateros stepping back but leaving a hand on his shoulder, squeezing, nodding at him with something that's so certainly approval and pride.

"Thank you," Mydei tells him, swallowing around the lump in his throat. "I am. Glad, that my mother had a friend like you."

Krateros smiles, chuckles a little. He squeezes Mydei's shoulder once more and steps back, returning to his spot by the fire. "Sit a while, if you have the time," he says. "I'm sure you could use the break."

"I..." His first instinct is to protest, but really, with the barricades already built and his body exhausted, what can he do but wait? "Very well," he says, and takes the seat opposite Krateros. "I suppose I could."

△

Night falls uneventfully. They have dinner. Mydei brings it to Anaxa, shaking him awake and listening to his murmurings as he eats. He takes care of Strife and the dromas after, then bathes just long enough to scrub the scent of the stables from his skin. He doubts he'll sleep, despite how tired he feels as he heads through the silent halls back to his room.

Still, stubbornly, even after changing the sheets, it smells like Phainon.

He tries not to think about it as he takes off his gauntlets—newly repaired by Chartonus—and leaves them within reach of the bed. He'll sleep in the rest of his armor, uncomfortable as it is, because putting it back on would take far too long in an emergency. He undoes the braid in his hair and shuts his eyes, breathing, sitting on the edge of the bed. 

Just a little longer, he tells himself, heavy. Leonnius' smile. Perdikkas'. Ptolemy's. He knows, between all of them, they can do this. It's just a matter of how and when.

There's a knock on the door, two soft raps, the second a little louder than the first. Mydei pulls his fingers through the now unbraided section of hair and stands, exhaling. It isn't a surprise when he opens the door and finds none other than Phainon, carrying Dawnmaker and looking like he doesn't belong.

"Hi," he says.

All his shadows in the poor lighting. Mydei traces the line of his jaw, the curl of hair standing straight up on his head. "Hi," he says back, and opens the door a little wider.

"I'm not supposed to be alone, and I figured, out of everyone here, it would be the least weird for me to share a room with you," Phainon explains himself, standing hesitantly.

"You've shared my bed twice already." Mydei reminds him, tired of the uncertain way he carries himself, tired of the uncertainty between them too. Their joined hands. Phainon's fingers in his hair. His scent sticking to all of Mydei's things. This feeling in his teeth. "Just come in."

So Phainon does, finding a spot to reverently place Dawnmaker before he comes to just... stand. Awkwardly, uncertainly, looking like he wants to apologize again. "HKS," Mydei says, and doesn't like the way he sounds fond, the way he is fond. "It's fine."

A soft, nervous laugh. "I feel like all I do is bother you and get in your space," Phainon tells him. "Every time you think you'll get a bit of space, here I am again. I'm—"

"Don't say it," Mydei cuts him off before he can apologize.

Again, one of those laughs. Phainon sits gingerly beside him on the bed. "...Sorry."

How many times has he forced Mydei to say these things aloud by now? How many times has Mydei given in? "If I minded your presence, don't you think I would've done something about it by now?" he asks. "Have I ever asked you to go?"

"No," Phainon says, after thinking about it. "I guess you haven't."

"And why do you think that is?" Mydei asks dryly, wondering if Phainon will ever really understand the answer.

"We're friends," Phainon says.

Mydei nods slowly. Even friends get tired of each other sometimes, he thinks, and wishes he had a better explanation for this. The feeling long since taken root in his chest. The handful of seeds Phainon scattered and left to grow without ever seeming to realize it.

"We are friends," he agrees, and wonders if Phainon thinks of them beyond just that, wonders if Phainon would run his fingers through Hephaestion's hair and hold Peucesta's hand too.

"When this is over," Phainon starts, wetting his lips, a little bit nervous, "can we stay that way? Can I stay your friend?"

"Do your friendships usually fizzle out so quickly?"

"Well. No," Phainon says, hooking a finger beneath his choker and snapping the strap lightly against his neck, gaze drifting around the room. "I just don't know what I would do if this one did."

His mouth, cracked and parted. Mydei looks away. "How you handle yourself is up to you," he says, instead of something stupid, like I want to stay in your life.

"You mean a lot to me," Phainon says, and it feels sudden, though maybe it isn't. "And I don't just mean that because you're helping me. I think... even if none of this ever happened, and it was just us on the road again, nothing to worry about, I would feel the same."

You mean a lot to me. The first time anyone has said those words to him. Phainon's hand on the bed, halfway between them. His awkward, audible swallow. He tends to be cold when Mydei touches him. What about now? What about the time after that? What would it take to keep him warm? "I wonder, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, if you hear the things that come out of your mouth."

"I mean it," Phainon tells him. He's looking when Mydei looks back. Determined about this as he is about getting stronger. "You've been an excellent friend to me, Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos."

Is that all this is? he imagines himself saying. Friendship?

Perhaps he's been starved of it. Winters spent with his brother and sister witchers, his friends, people who love him, and then the rest of the year spent without. Spent with wary, scared, hateful people who see him as a monster and a thing to be bought and disposed of shortly after. Maybe that's why this feels like more than friendship to him. Or maybe it's just them, just Phainon, and maybe he was always going to feel this way, regardless of anything else.

"You've been alright," he says, instead of any of that, and for some unfathomable reason, it makes Phainon laugh. It makes him laugh like he used to, before all of this. Bright as the midday sun, warm as it too. There are lines around his eyes that Mydei only notices now.

"Alright?" he repeats. "You think I'm alright, Mydeimos? Am I not your most kindred spirit? Your most treasured bosom friend, your—"

"Enough," Mydei says, and finds himself smiling too, if only a little. "You're remarkably adept at making light of the situation."

"It's a talent," Phainon says, grinning. Cracked lips, white teeth. His eyes. His lurid blue eyes, ringed with a shade as deep as the sea, reflecting the firelight. Titans above. Teasing, "All I'm hearing is that you think I'm remarkable."

"Remarkably idiotic," Mydei corrects. "Remarkably reckless, remarkably incorrigible, remarkably..."

Phainon leans forward and nods after each entry, smiling still, close-mouthed and enjoying this far too much, and Mydei... There are words for what he feels. There are words for what Phainon is and what he does to Mydei, but he won't say any of them. He can't... He doesn't think he could stand it, losing Phainon on top of everything else he already has. What is that called? What is this, that, any of it?

"Sure," he gives up and says, sighing, unable to help the way he wants Phainon to keep smiling. "You're remarkable."

"You almost make it sound like an insult," Phainon laughs. "Second thoughts, Mydeimos? Maybe you really are tired of me now."

Never and always. Mydei kicks off his shoes and lays all the way down, staying on the side of the bed closest to the wall so there's enough space for Phainon too. "I'm tired in general," he says. "Let me sleep. Or are you remarkably good at preventing that too?"

"Maybe I am," Phainon says, even as he stands to extinguish the lanterns keeping the room lit. Mydei watches him, eyes adjusting when the last one goes out and Phainon is left to feel his way back to the bed in the dark. He makes it, clearly unable to see a thing as he settles in carefully, smoothing a hand over the blanket until he bumps Mydei to gauge how much space he has. "There," he says, sliding beneath the sheets. "Bedtime."

"Don't steal the blankets," Mydei tells him. Their arms brush. Phainon has goosebumps.

"Me? I would never."

"Your track record isn't good," Mydei murmurs, watching him settle. Maybe it isn't fair, the way Mydei can see and Phainon can't. Maybe he shouldn't be watching, but what does it matter?

A soft laugh. Phainon turns to face him. "Sorry," he breathes, and he can't realize how close they are, can he? "Feel free to steal them back if I do." Or maybe he does, because his voice goes quiet and soft to match their proximity.

"You underestimate your vice grip," Mydei tells him, and finds his voice soft too. How easy it would be to touch him. His face or the side of his neck, beneath that choker he never takes off. His hand in Mydei's hair this morning, however long ago that was. Titans above. 

"I get cold, you know," Phainon says. He sounds like he's smiling, but he's hidden his mouth beneath the covers. "Not all of can walk around half-naked in the snow."

"When have I been half-naked in the snow?"

A chuckle, warm and soft already with sleep. "Rain," Phainon corrects himself. "The night we met."

"I was clothed."

"Oh, but your... conspicuous body was all out," Phainon says, muffled by fabric. "Do you ever wonder if that's why none of those villagers can look at you properly?"

"What?"

"Nothing, nothing." Phainon laughs. "Goodnight, Mydeimos. Wake me up if I steal the blankets."

"Goodnight," Mydei says back, too softly.

chapters.title: Chapter 17
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Phainon wakes up warm. Really, properly warm, not just warm so long as he keeps the blankets tight around him and doesn't move an inch to the left. It's still dark, he's entirely too comfortable; he isn't sure what woke him.

Awareness comes in stages. First, his body, the bed beneath him, the sheets. He cracks his eyes open and finds that he can't see much, only vague outlines in the dark. The back of Mydei's head, the mess of his hair, the wall. Slow, he turns onto his other side, sticky with sleep and unappreciative of the cold air slipping beneath the blanket as he moves.

His eyes slip shut. He breathes for a bit, nearly slipping back into sleep before that feeling, whatever it was that woke him up comes again. A prickle down his spine, something quick and sharp like a static shock. He blinks his eyes open and searches the dark of the room. Just shadows, all the lanterns put out. The dresser, Mydei's desk, Dawnmaker, propped against the wall.

Behind him, Mydei shifts, shoulder brushing Phainon's back. He's terribly warm. He's always so warm. Phainon closes his eyes.

Again, that feeling, that calling, something pulling at his chest. There's no sound, nothing that comes with it. Just silence. Mydei's breath. He blinks, stares at nothing, and feels that warmth and comfort shift into unease. He knows he won't be able to fall back asleep until he's eased his mind about whatever this is.

Quietly, so quietly, he lifts the blanket and edges out of bed, shivering at the immediate chill. The bed creaks. He pauses, watching Mydei for movement, but aside from the slow rise and fall of his breath, there is none. For how keen his senses are, for how light of a sleeper he usually is, somehow he doesn't notice this.

Again, Phainon's chest lurches. Something pulls. He finds his boots and steps into them as silently as he can, lifts Dawnmaker from where it's propped against the wall, and opens the door without a sound. One more glance in Mydei's direction and he slips out, shutting the door softly behind him.

The hall is dimly lit by nothing but the wall sconces, cold and silent but for the faint, occasional creaking of the as Castrum Kremnos moves. Phainon takes a shaky breath, cold hands tight on Dawnmaker's hilt, and starts down the hallway.

With each step, boots on carpeted stone, the chill stealing the sleep-warmth from his skin, his unease grows and grows. Go quietly, something in him says. Just get this over with.

He walks for all too long, palms sweating even as the cold bites at his fingers, and then he pushes the door open to the courtyard, wind whistling through the gap, a flurry of snow whipping him in the face. He squints against it, lifting one hand to shield his face as it stings his cheeks.

A blur of black, a metallic glint, a hand around his throat, seizing him and yanking him out of the doorway, lifting him up so he can only claw at a silver gauntlet and choke. Dawnmaker slips from his fingers. He can't breathe as the Flame Reaver raises him up.

"You," he says, rough as cutlery on ceramics, fingers tightening around the hilt of his wicked sword, "are nothing."

Phainon can barely kick, connecting with nothing but air. No matter how much he pulls and shoves and pries at the Flame Reaver's hand, it doesn't budge. He can't breathe—it's a kind of helplessness he isn't accustomed to. The strain on his throat, the pressure, the pain as he feels his windpipe crushed.

It's terror, terror is what climbs up his spine and floods his every nerve, but there's no outlet as he can't run, can't fight, can't breathe, can't even scream.

"Coward," the Flame Reaver hisses. "Hiding behind your witchers."

Phainon chokes, feels his vision blurring as he stares into that masked face, knowing what's beneath it, fingers growing weak from the lack of air.

"You'll always be weak," says the Flame Reaver, and then he raises his sword and plunges it straight through Phainon's abdomen. "You can't save anyone."

Blood, golden blood spills all over the crossguard of the sword, Phainon's every nerve alight with agony as his fingers curl over it, cold and slick with his own blood—gold, golden blood, and Phainon—

Phainon comes to with a gasp, still in bed, blanket half over him, one foot on the floor, already sitting up, one hand coming to his stomach, the other going for his throat. Nothing. He smooths his hands over fabric, hooks a finger in his choker. His pulse thunders. He breathes out, shaky, and drops his head to stare into his lap.

Pooled red fabric. Faint first morning light, not quite dawn. He inhales, hand still on his throat, feeling his heart beat, exhaling. Again, he squeezes his eyes shut, drags his other hand down his front, pressing his fingers into his sternum, between his ribs, finding it dry and unharmed. There's gooseflesh all over him.

"Titans above," he whispers.

The sheets rustle. The weight on the mattress shifts. Mydei, groggy and squinting when Phainon looks back at him. "Phainon?"

"A nightmare," Phainon breathes, as much to himself as to Mydei. He's sweating. It's cold, he's shaking. "Just a nightmare. Nothing to worry about."

A hand curls around his elbow, warm as anything, tugging lightly. "It's still early," Mydei grumbles, so Phainon eases carefully back into bed and under the covers, their shoulders brushing as they lay side by side.

"Sorry," he says, pulling the blanket back up. "I didn't mean to wake you."

"HKS," is the reply, soft as Mydei breathes in deep, turning toward him. "You reek of fear sweat."

"I..." A nervous laugh. Mydei's still holding his arm. "Sorry?"

A long exhale. Mydei's brow presses into his shoulder, and he goes still, not quite sure what to do with himself. "What did you see?" Mydei asks, breath warm through the fabric of Phainon's shirt.

"Just. The Flame Reaver. He choked and stabbed me, nothing... nothing much." But every detail had been so vivid. He'd felt the cold, he'd felt the pain, the crushing of his windpipe, the parting of his flesh. The blood, his blood, his gold blood. Why wasn't it red?

"It's only natural that you'd dream of it," Mydei murmurs. He sounds half asleep. His head presses harder into Phainon's shoulder, hand still curled in his elbow. Does he realize how close he is, or is he too sleep-addled to notice? Phainon's heart still thunders so hard he can feel it. He wonders if Mydei's strong senses can hear that too. "Do you want me to cast a Sign?"

"No," Phainon says, folding a hand over his heart, shutting his eyes and calming his breath. "No, I'm— I'm alright, thank you."

A low hum. Minutes later, Mydei drifts back into sleep. Phainon lays there. A little longer, and it'll be dawn. A little longer, he'll just rest his eyes. Mydei's breath is soft. His heart calms. A little longer, he'll just...

△

At breakfast, things are normal enough. He receives half smiles and greetings that he gives back. A bowl of Chartonus' latest culinary creation in front of each of them, they share some slightly stilted conversation. It feels too quiet without Ptolemy there. Mydei, Peucesta, Krateros, Castorice, and Chartonus are all fairly soft spoken. Hephaestion seems too tired to project his usual energy and Phainon... Can't, with the rest of them like this.

Guilt weighs him down, no matter how much they all try to convince him that none of this is his fault. He forces himself to eat everything in his bowl, if only so he'll have the energy for training, if only so he can recover and stay as strong as he can. He's still sore all over. Maybe that's just the cold, the morning, but he needs to be at his best.

When he's finished eating, he stands to wash his bowl and return it to the kitchen, still within sight of the group of witchers. But the moment he passes through the door to the kitchen, propped open, a hand seizes him by the throat.

"You're nothing," says the Flame Reaver, lifting him up as again Phainon chokes and scrambles at that hand and feels himself flooded with fear as his lungs refuse to fill. "You'll never be safe. Neither will they, as long as you're alive."

He can't make a sound beyond this awful, muted gurgling to grab anyone's attention. Through the doorway, he can see them still talking and eating breakfast, not one of them looking this way. They're witchers, why can't they hear, why don't they notice? Trying to gasp in breath, trying to pull the Flame Reaver's hand from his throat, he feels his vision start to blacken, pain and pressure blurring his senses. He'd left Dawnmaker at the table.

"Coward. Still hiding behind them," the Flame Reaver hisses. "Who should I kill next? The ailing one, already wasting away? The girl? The lion of which you're so fond?" His hand grows tighter and tighter, crushing, Phainon's vision fading, his body going weak. The Flame Reaver raises his sword, setting the tip of it right between Phainon's ribs. "All of them, one by one as you watch?"

With a quick motion, the Flame Reaver slides the blade home, the sound sickening, blood pouring—gold blood pouring—the pain white-hot and blinding, Phainon unable to do anything but—

He stumbles and catches himself on the floor, the bowl flying from his hand and breaking into a dozen pieces as he fights to catch his breath. The bowl, the bowl, he hadn't had the bowl when the Flame Reaver grabbed him. He wasn't stabbed, he wasn't choked. He can breathe, nothing in him hurts but his knee where it slammed into the ground and there's no blood, no bruises, no nothing. Another dream, another curse, another—

"Phainon!"

A group of worried faces. They'd all come running. Mydei, expression hard and searching. Castorice, keeping her distance. Peucesta and Krateros, swords in hand. Even Chartonus stands behind them all. Hephaestion, hiding a cough in the pit of his elbow. The ailing one, already wasting away. Phainon is going to be sick.

"I'm—" His heart thunders. He squeezes his eyes shut, yanks all of his pieces back together. Shards of ceramic all over. The phantom of pressure where he'd imagined the Flame Reaver holding him by the throat. "I tripped," he finds himself saying, trying to stand. "I'm so sorry, I didn't—"

"Careful," Mydei hisses, yanking his arm before he can put his hand down on a broken piece of the bowl. Swallowing, Phainon stands, carefully this time.

"I'm sorry about the bowl," he says, looking at each of them in turn. He's not sure if they believe him. He's not sure if he believes himself. "I'll... I'll clean it up. Again, I'm—"

"Okay, it is," Chartonus says. "Many bowls in Castrum Kremnos."

"Thank you," Phainon says, swallowing. He brings a hand to his throat, hoping the way he plays with his choker comes off as embarrassed over taking a fall and creating a commotion rather than whatever it actually is that he's feeling. Lingering terror as he checks that there's no bruising or breakage, something haunting as he presses his fingers into his pulse to make sure his heart is still beating. "I'll just..."

He squats, starting to collect the broken pieces on the floor as the rest of them bends to help too. They're sharp, but he's careful as he gathers them up, the vision replaying over and over in his head. The sword through his ribs, the pain, the golden blood.

The next piece he grabs he presses into the pad of his thumb, just to see, just to be sure. A slight sting. It wells up red, and he exhales, blanketed in this odd, bone-deep relief.

Peucesta grabs the last piece, careful with slender, musical fingers.

"Thank you," Phainon tells them all, bowing his head, embarrassed for real this time as his heart finally calms and his breath comes back to him. "Sorry again."

"You cut yourself," says Hephaestion, reaching for his free hand, thumb smeared with red.

Phainon pretends to only notice this now. "Oh," he says, and laughs a little, awkward, nervous. "It seems I did."

△

He pours himself into his training, having been banned from it the day before. He learns from Castorice, Hephaestion, Peucesta, and Mydei in turn, sparring and practicing technique after technique with ample rest in between. He's cut off after a while so he won't overwork himself again, flushed and out of breath, sweat freezing in the cold.

When the adrenaline runs dry, there's nothing to keep his mind off his worries, so he finds Krateros and runs through slow, rhythmic, meditative sword forms in the courtyard, Mydei within sight, Strife and the dromas playing outside in his care. It isn't strenuous, but the concentration and the emphasis on controlling his breath makes it count as a form of training the rest of them can't object to.

It's hard, keeping his brain quiet. Krateros can't cast the Sign of Cerces and call it a day; instead it's all in concentration and mental conditioning. He practices with a wooden training sword instead of Dawnmaker, so it's light and untiring, but the hilt in his hand, the motions through the air like water, the footwork, all of it gives him something to focus on. His breath, in, out. The tiredness in his muscles, the sting of the cold. He watches Krateros' back and carefully follows his every motion.

After a time, he memorizes the motions enough to shut his eyes as he slides through them. He turns all his attention inward, and feels that familiar restlessness calm, the fire within him softening to warm embers. Time passes like this. The next time he opens his eyes, Krateros is still, just watching him.

Phainon eases out of his stance, controlled and fluid, bringing the sword to rest at his side, feet square, exhaling a deep breath. He swallows, still aware of himself down to the fingertips, bows and says, "Thank you, Lord Krateros."

A sigh. Krateros' laugh is a little bit rough with his age. He reaches for Phainon's training sword and returns it with his own to the weapon rack. "You're a good man, son," he says when it's done, laying his hand on Phainon's clueless shoulder. "I suppose I owe you an apology."

Phainon blinks. "I... Sorry. Thank you. Pardon?"

"You're a honest man in a bad situation," Krateros says. "I have seen better men break for less, and here you are, still trying your utmost to fight. I've been unfair to you."

Phainon stares at him. His graying hair, the scar over his blind eye, his tired, weathered face. "I don't understand," Phainon tries.

"I have waited a long time for the Son of Gorgo," Krateros says, patting him once, squeezing, and stepping back. "As such, perhaps I have been too critical of your influence on him. But I see now that you aren't a bad match for him."

"I..." Mydei in the background, tossing a rubber ball for the dromas to chase and bring back for him to throw it again. It replays in his head, you aren't a bad match for him, again and again. Mydei, the strongest person he's met. Phainon, his match. His face heats. He swallows thickly. "It means a lot to hear you say that," he says, returning his attention to Krateros, extending a hand for him to shake. "Really, I... Thank you, sir. I am certainly trying my best."

Another laugh. "No need to put so much weight to my words," Krateros tells him, clasping his hand. "But... You're welcome."

"Yeah," Phainon says, and finds his nose running from the cold. "I... Hah." He rubs at the back of his neck. "And thank you for your help with the sword. You've taught me a lot and I appreciate that too."

Krateros smiles, claps him on the shoulder again. "You're welcome, son," he says, and this feeling climbs up Phainon's throat. "I'm rooting for you."

"Thank—" Phainon clears his throat. "I've said that a lot, haven't I? I won't let you down, sir. For the sake of everyone here."

"Krateros," comes the correction.

"Krateros," Phainon repeats, straightening up. "I won't let you down."

Krateros laughs through his nose. "For now, you're due for a rest. And a bath."

He's sweat-soaked and dirty from his training, hours now since he began. The cuffs of his pants are caked in mud and wet from melted snow. "You're right," he says. "I— You— Well."

"I suppose I could go for a soak in the springs as well," Krateros says before he can continue to flounder. "Get your things and we'll go."

"Right, of course," Phainon says, nodding three times before he forces himself to stop. He leads the way back to the door inside, pulling it open for Krateros to pass through first, but no sooner is the door halfway open before he's grabbed by the throat and yanked through.

"Coward," the Flame Reaver hisses again. "You'll never be safe."

Phainon makes an awful sound as he chokes, the sensation of pressure around his throat familiar by now as he pries as the Flame Reaver's fingers and tries to look back, the door now shut.

"All you bring is ruin." He draws his sword arm back, but this time Phainon is prepared, planting a foot against the Flame Reaver's chest and trying to shove—

That wicked sword plunges through him again, parting flesh, breaking through bone, hot, golden blood pouring down the blade. "Everyone around you will die."

Phainon opens his eyes to an empty doorway, heart thundering, knees weak. He catches himself on the door, accidentally slamming it shut.

"Phainon?" Krateros, behind him, confused and concerned and clearly not having seen the same things Phainon has. This is another curse. It has to be. Phainon presses his hand into his intact abdomen and forces himself to breathe. The Flame Reaver knows he can't win by brute force. Not yet, not without Phainon's fear. Instead, he's—

Titans above. He's here. He's been here, he's just been quiet about it.

"I'm alright," Phainon says, and somehow his heart manages to calm. This is his strength, his power. He has control over this much, now that he understands. One more breath. He'll banish his fear. He'll know what to expect, and this time, no one will get hurt.

"Are you certain?" Krateros asks, coming up behind him and laying a hand on his shoulder.

"I am," Phainon confirms, and finds it as true as it can be. "But I need to talk with Mydei and the rest. The springs will have to wait a bit."

△

"They're visions like the one he gave me back in that village," Phainon explains. "They're too real to be nightmares or hallucinations. I feel it all, and he's— He's getting stronger from them. But he has to be nearby to cast whatever spells, right? He can't just..."

"He has to be inside," Mydei confirms, and leans his mouth against his hands, arms propped on the table that the seven of them can't fill. Phainon lets out a breath, Hephaestion a colorful curse.

"He's weak," Phainon says, convincing himself of it as much as them. "That's why he's trying it this way instead of an actual confrontation. One moment I'll be doing whatever and the next he'll grab me by the throat in one of those visions, say some awful things, and then he'll stab me, and I'll blink and I'm back in the real world. He's just. He's trying to scare me without crossing all of you so he can build up strength before another fight, I'm sure of it."

Glances around the table. "That's what happened at breakfast, isn't it?" Peucesta asks softly.

"It was," Phainon agrees. "But I was... shaken and couldn't get myself to say anything when I should have been honest. This... This concerns all of you as much as does me. If he's getting stronger..." He lowers his head, staring at the grain of the table, the swirling knots in the wood he's tempted to trace with his fingers. "I'm sorry."

"We need to put a stop to this," Castorice says.

Mydei leans back in his chair, crossing his arms over his chest. "Where is Anaxa when we need him?" He gives a rough, almost bitter laugh. "None of us are sorcerers."

"Try Phagousa's Sign, you might," Chartonus suggests.

Hephaestion shakes his head. "No; that might work to shake him out of the visions as they're occurring, but it sounds like they're fast. He wasn't gone long at all before he dropped the bowl this morning."

"He only seemed to pause for a breath at the door this most recent time," Krateros adds. 

"So they're fast," says Mydei. "Phagousa's Sign won't work. None of us are sorcerers to counteract the spell, and the Flame Reaver is actively roaming the halls laying traps."

"We need to find him now, while he's still weak," Castorice says.

Phainon curls his hands into fists on his thighs, replaying the memory in his head, the pain, the agony, the Flame Reaver's threats. He finds himself, rather than afraid, viciously angry. "I'll be ready this time," he says, nails digging hard into his palms. "I've already felt what he can do to me, and I'm not scared of it anymore. Next time I walk into one of his traps, he won't get anything from me."

"Good," Mydei says, simple as that. They meet eyes across the table, and he isn't smiling, not quite, but he nods with something like approval, and another sensation joins the hot fury in his chest. Phainon nods back.

"One more thing," he says. "In these visions, I bleed gold like one of you, or... like him..."

There's a brief silence as everyone thinks. "He wears your face, does he not?" Peucesta cuts through it.

"He does."

"The moment you were born, he all but became your clone, at least in appearance. He looks like you, so perhaps he assumes you bleed gold like he does when he sends you these visions."

"In any case," Mydei adds, "the distinction will help tell illusion from reality. If you bleed gold, there's nothing to fear."

Difficult, considering he doesn't see the gold until he's been stabbed, but, well. Phainon lets out a breath. "Alright," he says. Again, "Alright. I'll be ready."

△

Predictably, the moment Phainon steps out of the dining hall—sandwiched in the middle of the group on the off chance that the Flame Reaver's traps might be non-specific and one of the witchers could suffer them for him instead—there's a blur of black and a hand in a silver gauntlet reaching out. He knows it isn't real even as he dives out of the way, Dawnmaker heavy in his hands, faced with that terrifying masked figure, this time he feels nothing but angry. The witchers, his friends all continue walking down the hall, and that's how he knows there isn't a shred of reality in the Flame Reaver's scenario. They would never, never leave him alone like this.

"You're weak," he says as the Flame Reaver turns to him after the failed grab, lifting his sword. Rage boils in his chest as he stands up tall, gritting his teeth. "Otherwise you wouldn't bother with any of this. Between us, who's the real coward?"

"You think yourself strong," the Flame Reaver rasps. "You've played around with witchers and fancy yourself one of them. But how could you be, after killing one of their number with your own hands?"

"That was you," Phainon grits. His hands go white-knuckled on Dawnmaker's hilt. "You killed Ptolemy. You killed my family and burnt down my home. All of that was you!" He lunges forward, bringing Dawnmaker in an arc, feeling it in his teeth as the Flame Reaver catches the blade with his own.

"I couldn't have done it without your help," says the Flame Reaver. "You, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, Phainon of Ash and Bloodshed, are my greatest accomplice."

A raw sound rips through Phainon's throat as he throws the force between their blades to the side, knocking the Flame Reaver's sword hand off balance and immediately trying for another attack. The monster disappears from in front of him and appears again behind, plunging his sword straight through Phainon's back. A sharp jolt of fear runs through him as he isn't fast enough the react, and then the agony splits him in half.

"Next," says the Flame Reaver, "the lion."

It climbs up his throat, chokes him. The version of Mydei in the vision turns the corner. Hot fury turns to cold, cold terror. Phainon looks down to see the blade parting his flesh, the river of gold as he loses the strength in his legs and crashes to his knees, ripping himself open further, vision blurring from the pain.

"He makes your fear taste especially sweet," the Flame Reaver tells him. His foot presses into Phainon's back as he rips out the sword.

A scream tears from Phainon's throat, the agony blinding, the terror left with nowhere else to go, and—

Someone bumps into his back.

"Phainon?" Mydei coming out behind him, his hand on Phainon's shoulder blade; he must've stopped in his tracks when he stumbled into that vision. Now, he looks down at his own front, dirty and sweat-soaked from his training, but intact. His heart beats in his ears. He finds Castorice and Peucesta, who left the room first, looking back at him.

"Again, Lord Phainon?" Castorice asks, eyebrows drawing together.

Phainon lets out a shaky breath. "Again," he confirms. "I'm— I'm alright. He did manage to scare me a little when he stabbed me again, but..." He laughs nervously. Nobody joins him. When he turns to glance at Mydei, Hephaestion, Krateros, Chartonus, there are only concerned looks all around.

Hephaestion lays a hand on his shoulder. "I don't suppose you'll agree to hole up in your room for a while while we do a thorough sweep of the place?"

"That won't work." Phainon shakes his head, blinking hard as he forces himself back into reality. "He's too smart; you won't find him if I'm not there with you."

"Worth a shot, at least," Hephaestion says, smiling a little, squeezing his shoulder.

Phainon squeezes his eyes shut and hears the Flame Reaver's voice again. The lion, next. He pulls his determination back, squeezes it tight in his fist like a lifeline. He can't let this happen. He can't let the Flame Reaver get stronger, he can't let Mydei—let any of them—get hurt. Next time, next time he won't feel any fear at all.

"It seems," Krateros says after a long silence, "that now isn't a good time for a bath after all."

△

It happens again halfway down the hall, again at the entrance to the armory, where they arm themselves to the teeth, again, again, again if he dares move so much as a step. Each time, Phainon fights back more and more. Each time, he grows angrier and angrier as the Flame Reaver spews threat after threat. Each time, inevitably, he ends up stabbed again, through the back, through the chest, stomach, once through the throat. It hurts like it's real every time, but then he returns to real life and he returns furious.

This time, he comes back gasping, catching himself hard on one knee and pressing himself right back up, seething, one hand curled tight around Dawnmaker's hilt, the other a fist, boiling over.

"Coward!" he screams into empty, hollow halls. He hears his own echo come back, and knows that somewhere, somewhere within these walls, the Flame Reaver is watching and can hear him. "You coward, hiding behind your illusions!" The words take all his breath. He realizes he's shaking, sweat from the stress of encounter after encounter dripping down his back.

"Phainon," says Peucesta gently, the one guarding Phainon now while the other witchers try to search the fortress. He must see it in Phainon's eyes, he must smell the way he doesn't reek of fear, just anger, rage, fury. He straightens all the way up, panting for breath.

"Stand up, and face me, Executioner!" Phainon shouts, forcing the sweat-soaked hair out of his face and shifting Dawnmaker into a two-handed grip. His own voice echoes back as he waits, scanning the shadows and finding nothing, not even a flicker of black or a glint of metal, not a thing to prove the source of his madness is really there.

A frustrated scream tears from his throat. He lowers Dawnmaker and stands there, enraged and out of breath, squeezing his eyes shut and remembering the pain, the Flame Reaver's latest string of threats. He's trembling. He wants to scream again. He can't stop himself. When he stops to listen, it's just quiet, and the fight slips out of him all at once.

Peucesta is patient as Phainon gets a hold of himself, sighing and straightening up, switching Dawnmaker to his other hand to stretch out the tired muscles in his palm.

"Sorry, I don't know what's wrong with me," he breathes, and turns just in time to see the Flame Reaver run Peucesta through.

"You wanted to face me?" the Flame Reaver asks, pulling the blade free with his boot on Peucesta's back for leverage. There's a sickening sound, golden blood splattering faded red carpets and stone. Peucesta is silent as he goes down, only staring down at the hole in his chest before he crumples to the ground. "You think you're so strong that you don't need to fear me now?"

"Go, Phainon," Peucesta finally chokes out, curling a hand over his bleeding middle, trying to push himself up with the other, his face twisting with effort. "Get... the others..."

Blood drips from the Flame Reaver's blade, wicked and glinting in the light. Masked, faceless and towering, he points the blade at Peucesta again. "I can show you real fear."

Phainon's hands curl tight around Dawnmaker as he raises it up again, forcing himself into a fighting stance. "Leave him out of this," he says, voice trembling, heart thundering in his ears, realizing he's shaking again. Is it fear that he feels, gaze stuck on Peucesta? It can't be. It can't be too late to save him, not when they have Signs and magic and—

Not when this isn't even real. Another of the Flame Reaver's visions, targeting the others because Phainon is no longer afraid of empty threats and being targeted himself. The Flame Reaver is weak, he reminds himself. He's desperate and hungry and has already proven himself too much of a coward to face them properly.

The fight in him comes right back. He stands tall and he feels no fear in the face of this monster. He's fought him before in vision after vision. He's endured all of that pain, growing less and less afraid each time, and this time, in this vision too, he knows he doesn't need to be afraid at all.

Dawnmaker is the perfect weight in his hands, the blade beautifully sharp and untested, waiting for this, waiting for whenever he might have this chance to fight back for real. This, and all the practice runs before it will only serve to make him stronger, more familiar with the Flame Reaver's patterns and weaknesses. He'll endure this pain as many times as it takes.

"This is between you and me, Executioner," he growls, voice as low and angry as he's ever heard it. "I'm the one you want. Why bother with all of this?"

The Flame Reaver seems to consider him, lifting his sword from where it's pointed at Peucesta's neck. He abandons the witcher, still bleeding all over the floor, passed out now, hauntingly realistic as all of this is, as all of this has been. It serves only to make Phainon's fury grow. The disregard for all these these lives, the insistence upon hurting and taking and destroying all for the sake of what? A little bit of fear, a little bit of power. What kind of parasite attacks more than just its host? He's burning down Phainon's entire world for scraps, and It isn't fair, it's never been fair, and Phainon has been so furious for such a long time.

The Flame Reaver comes closer, step by echoing step. His free hand lifts to remove his mask, pushing his hood back with it so Phainon is forced to stare into his own face and wonder if it's really possible for him to wear an expression so cruel and monstrous.

"You forget," says the Flame Reaver, smiling wickedly—Phainon's face, but not his face at all. "All of this, we do together. I'll help you remember."

"Never," Phainon says, standing his ground. Again, his voice rising, "Never!"

The Flame Reaver swings first, blade slicing through the air as Phainon leaps out of the way. He isn't scared, he tells himself, shifting Dawnmaker in his grip. He has nothing to be afraid of as he blocks a second blow, metal screaming against metal.

Dawnmaker doesn't break or chip, the most beautifully crafted weapon he's held in his hands, crafted and weighted perfectly to suit him. It feels solid, perfect, right. Gritting his teeth, staring into his own twisted face, a rough sound tearing from his throat, he throws off the Flame Reaver's blade and swings Dawnmaker down in a short arc onto his shoulder.

The Flame Reaver catches it with his other hand, unsteady from the force, an awful sound coming from the collision of sword and gauntlet. He smiles cruelly with Phainon's face. "Is this your best?" he asks, gripping the blade tighter when Phainon tries to pull it away. Golden blood wells up from the Flame Reaver's palm, a drop sliding along the edge of the blade toward the hilt, but he doesn't react.

"Is this all there is to the strength of a hero?"

Phainon tries for a kick as he wrenches Dawnmaker from the Flame Reaver's hand, leveraging himself on it to cut deeper as his foot slams into the Flame Reaver's side. He doesn't even flinch, but lets the sword go and Phainon is able to put space between them.

"Is this all there is to the strength of a monster?" Phainon shoots back. Another clash of swords, Phainon parrying, watching the blood from the Flame Reaver's cut hand smear all over his hilt as Phainon isn't afraid enough to heal him. "Cheap tricks and illusions, hurting the people I care about, is that all that you're capable of?" he all but shouts.

Metal screams against metal. This time, he manages to overpower the Flame Reaver, catching him in the shoulder, tearing that already tattered cloak. Gold wells up. Phainon's whole body is alight with adrenaline and fury.

"You're weak!" A vicious downstrike, all of Phainon's strength in the blow to end all of this, to finally free himself from this torment, this cruelty. He'll have a shred of justice, he thinks, finally, even if it's only in this vision, and then the shadows warp and blur and his blade connects with nothing at all.

A hand seizes him by the throat, raises him up, and it's so familiar by now that he knows exactly what comes next.

"Such foolishness to think you don't need to be afraid," the Flame Reaver says, squeezing tighter, crushing. Phainon loses his grip on Dawnmaker, can hardly hear it fall to the ground through the roaring of the blood in his ears.

He can't breathe. It hurts and it hurts and it hurts, but it's familiar, his hand on the Flame Reaver's wrist, his lungs screaming for air, the pain in his throat, the blood in his head. There's nothing to be afraid of, he knows. He can live through this one more time. He knows he'll come out again on the other side.

"I will show you fear," the Flame Reaver threatens. "I will show you pain and suffering and bloodshed."

Do your worst, Phainon thinks. He can't get the words out as his vision blackens around the edges and his muscles go weak with lack of oxygen. His lungs scream. He forces a smile, and feels the Flame Reaver grow enraged in the way his grip constricts tighter, crushing his windpipe.

"Your friends, your lion can wait," the Flame Reaver growls. "You've forgotten what it means to suffer. Let me remind you."

The feeling of the Flame Reaver's blade is familiar too, slamming home between his ribs. The agony is white hot as he feels it carve through him, sharp and crooked and coming out his back. No matter how many times he lives this part, it always hurts more than anything, blinding him, a strangled sound leaving him with the last of his breath.

"You'll die here," the Flame Reaver tells him, twisting the blade— twisting, tearing through already torn flesh. It hurts, it hurts and it feels real, and Phainon can't breathe, can't think, can't feel any of the strength in his limbs. "You'll die here, and everyone you care about will come after. Rest assured, I will leave no survivors."

Violently, viciously, the Flame Reaver tears his sword out, covered in red gore. "This," he says, throwing Phainon down, the impact redoubling the pain as he struggles to even gasp for breath with his insides torn open, "is your end, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae."

His vision is blurred with tears, still black at the edges, fading rapidly. When he looks down, it's to the mess of his front, pain stealing the sense in his head, lungs trying and failing over and over again to fill. Blood, pain everywhere. It's all he can see, it's all he can feel. 

The glint of the Flame Reaver's boots, smeared in red. Red, red, red. He can't wait for this to be over. Can't wait to wake as a kick slams into his stomach, torn and bleeding and red, red, red. He can't think through the pain, through the ringing in his ears, through the tears in his eyes and the blackness in his vision.

Red, there's so much red. Why isn't this over yet?

Another kick. His back slams against the wall. He sees his own crimson drag path on carpet and stone. His sight swims. There's blood all over the hand he tries to leverage beneath himself. Red blood.

It's only then, as his sight and senses slip from him, as he must die, that he realizes that this must be real.

The last thing he feels before he loses it all is pure, unadulterated terror.
